clue.text: Would it take another like him to be of one mind?

definitions.text: Would it take another like him to be of one mind?

parts.words: Would it take another like him to be of one mind?
parts.note: a person with half a brain would need a second such person to add up to one complete mind

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether two people would agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of one mind' usually means in agreement; here it means owning one whole mind, which two halves would make.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit is jokingly said to have only half the usual intelligence, hence the name.

clue.text: Gathers crowds when speaking

indicators.note: signals the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: hordes are large crowds

explanation.surface: Someone draws a crowd whenever they make a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To stockpile or amass is to gather and store things, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Incline towards getting a simple building

parts.note: to lean is to incline
to means towards

explanation.surface: Leaning towards building something simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A basic shed built against a wall, with a sloping roof, is a simple structure.

clue.text: Stream of notes by Handel?

parts.note: a stream is a body of water
notes make up music

explanation.surface: A flow of melody composed by Handel.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Handel's suite as one example of a stream of notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel wrote a famous orchestral suite for a royal barge trip on the Thames.

clue.text: Try to have discrimination

definitions.meaning: to try food is to sample it
refined judgement in matters of style

explanation.surface: Advice to attempt to be discerning.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample food, and also refined aesthetic judgement.

clue.text: Hire one to play the female lead

indicators.note: the letters are made to perform in a new arrangement, as an actor plays a part

explanation.surface: A casting director is told to hire someone for the leading lady role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play' rearranges HIREONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal female character of a story or film is its main woman, the starring part.

clue.text: Misery of a teacher working with horrible head

indicators.note: the head of the word horrible is its first letter
the letters are set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher toiling under a dreadful headmaster is miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible head' is the head (first letter) of horrible; 'working' shuffles 'a teacher' to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional pain or grief is a kind of misery.

clue.text: Teases wool in rows

definitions.meaning: to tease someone is to mock them playfully
in knitting, raised ridges of wool in rows

explanation.surface: Someone mocks wool laid out in lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful mocking, and also raised ridged rows in knitted fabric.

clue.text: One's not afraid to speak — probably!

definitions.meaning: a person who dares to say something
a hedging phrase meaning I suppose so

explanation.surface: A bold person probably speaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase is one (I) who dares say.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means I suppose or very likely, and literally one daring to speak.

clue.text: Object about wrong-doers being supported

parts.note: an end is an object or aim

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An objection about criminals receiving support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link meaning concerning; 'wrong' rearranges DOERS into ORSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Backed or approved is the meaning of this past participle.

clue.text: Fit girl given body-building exercises

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
PT stands for physical training

explanation.surface: A fit young woman is given a workout programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like an adjective about the girl but is a verb meaning adjust.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit something to a purpose is to modify or adjust it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Right to get outstanding performer on committee

parts.note: a star is a leading performer
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: Someone claims a right to put a celebrity on a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the right-hand side when facing forward has its own nautical name.

clue.text: Cleaners put off by public convenience

parts.note: to deter someone is to put them off
the gents is a men's public toilet in British usage

explanation.surface: Cleaners are put off by having to work in a public toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: GENTS is the British name for a men's public lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing powders and liquids are cleaning agents, products used for cleaning.

clue.text: Better the non-drinker leaves this

indicators.note: the word for the abstainer departs from the word before it, so it is taken out

parts.note: TT means teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: A teetotaller is advised to stay away from alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing TT from BETTER leaves the drink a non-drinker avoids, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer by definition refuses alcoholic drinks such as ale or lager.

clue.text: Farmed in a civilised way

definitions.meaning: land prepared and used for crops

explanation.surface: Land worked in a refined manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilled land, and also refined, educated manners.

clue.text: Spirit conjured up by other spirits?

definitions.text: Spirit conjured up by other spirits?

parts.words: Spirit conjured up by other spirits?
parts.note: courage (spirit) brought on by drinking alcohol (spirits), not a ghost summoned by ghosts

explanation.surface: A ghost summoned by other ghosts at a seance.
explanation.walkthrough: The supernatural reading of 'spirit' and 'conjured' misleads; it is bravery induced by liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery gained from alcohol is called this, after a supposed Dutch habit of drinking gin before battle.

clue.text: It may be tipped but not recommended by doctors

definitions.text: It may be tipped but not recommended by doctors

parts.words: It may be tipped but not recommended by doctors
parts.note: a filter-tipped smoke that doctors advise against, not a horse tipped to win

explanation.surface: A racing tip that medics advise against.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' suggests a racing tip; it means filter-tipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A filter-tipped smoke is harmful, so doctors advise against it.

clue.text: A bed made badly, George Eliot's work

indicators.note: the letters are made badly, into a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A badly made bed in the home of a Victorian novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: George Eliot was a Victorian novelist; this is her first full-length novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Her 1859 novel about a carpenter is one of George Eliot's works.

clue.text: No townsperson having beer after 6.50

indicators.note: the drink comes after the numerals

parts.note: 6 is VI in Roman numerals and 50 is L
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A country dweller drinks a beer at ten to seven.
explanation.walkthrough: '6.50' looks like a time but is Roman numerals VI and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in a small rural settlement is not a town dweller.

clue.text: They get passed on the road

definitions.text: They get passed on the road

parts.words: They get passed on the road
parts.note: examinations a learner passes while driving on the road, not vehicles overtaken

explanation.surface: Slow vehicles get overtaken on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed' suggests overtaking; it means succeeding in an exam taken on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical examinations for a licence to drive are taken out on public roads.

clue.text: Reach a swirling river

indicators.note: the letters swirl round like eddying water into a new order

explanation.surface: Arriving at an eddying river.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to get there, a verb synonym.

clue.text: It checks the growth of population

definitions.text: It checks the growth of population

parts.words: It checks the growth of population
parts.note: it counts how many people there are, rather than restraining their increase

explanation.surface: A measure such as birth control restrains population growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checks' suggests curbing; it means counting.
explanation.definitionFit: An official count of the population checks its numbers periodically.

clue.text: Mail goes astray in country

indicators.note: the letters wander off course into a new order

explanation.surface: Post gets lost somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked West African republic is a country.

clue.text: New stars never cross

indicators.note: the letters are made new, formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Freshly discovered stars never meet each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning lying across.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying crosswise, at right angles to an axis, is described this way.

clue.text: She tends to rush over certain points

indicators.note: the word for rush is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: to run is to rush
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: A woman tends to hurry through particular matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She tends to' reads as a habit; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer in a hospital looks after the sick, tending to them.

clue.text: University chaps, first that'll be ordered off

indicators.note: the chaps come first, ahead of the university letter

parts.note: men are chaps

explanation.surface: University men, first in line, are sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered off' suggests being sent away; it means choosing dishes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of dishes is what diners order from in a restaurant.

clue.text: A whisker

parts.note: something that whisks, a kitchen tool, rather than a hair on the face

explanation.walkthrough: 'whisker' reads as a hair; it is a thing that whisks.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool used to whisk eggs is one that whisks, a literal agent noun.

clue.text: Call of captain for ends?

definitions.meaning: at the toss of a coin before a match a captain calls heads or this
rear parts or ends, as of a coat or an animal

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket and other sports, captains call the coin toss before play.
explanation.definitionFit: One face of a coin called at the toss, and also the back ends of things.

clue.text: Bound for Rouen, perhaps, with a note

indicators.note: signals the city name is just a possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone travelling to a French city carries a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ROUEN into ENROU.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning on the way to a destination, heading towards it.

clue.text: Not interrupted without purpose

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
less means lacking, as in a suffix

explanation.surface: An activity carries on uninterrupted, though with no point to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unceasing goes on and on, with no break or stop.
